boundary: Manual descriptions support the implemented subset. Unit tests establish prototype behavior only; no fresh compiler or controller validation was performed.

rules.implemented: Reference binding inherits both caller array length and physical element capacity; forwards the same storage.
rules.restriction: Whole-array assignment requires identical concrete length and element capacity. Different-capacity whole-array conversion is blocked.

rules.implemented: Positive one-based start and positive count; exact in-range copies of at most 254 characters; a start after the current source length returns empty.
rules.restriction: In-range requests extending past the current source end and results longer than 254 are blocked pending source/runtime evidence. Destination assignment applies its existing physical bound.

rules.implemented: Returns the one-based position of the first exact occurrence, or zero when absent.
rules.restriction: An empty search string is blocked. ASCII-only source and search values.

rules.implemented: Returns one ASCII character for integer codes 0 through 127, including controls.
rules.restriction: Other codes and alternate character sets are blocked; Python Unicode conversion is not treated as a KAREL mapping.

rules.implemented: Returns the ASCII code at a one-based index; rejects indexes outside the current string length.
rules.restriction: ASCII only. Index errors use KarelRuntimeError, not KAREL task pause/alarm behavior.

rules.implemented: ASCII logical values of at most 254 characters pass by independent initialized copy to formals with no direct/transitive potential writes; nested bare forwarding retains runtime write protection.
rules.restriction: Physical capacity is deliberately unspecified. Writable STRING value temporaries and STRING routine results remain blocked; see string_value_semantics.json.

unresolved.finding: The manual permits temporary copying but does not establish physical capacity for subsequent writes. Read-only copies now avoid using or guessing that capacity.
unresolved.disposition: E_STRING_VALUE when a target formal may be written; read-only value inputs and existing reference arguments are supported.

unresolved.finding: No discriminating controller observations were obtained for empty INDEX searches or SUB_STR requests extending past the current source end.
unresolved.disposition: Explicit runtime rejection; no Python slice-clipping or empty-search rule is assumed.

unresolved.finding: The string-operator chapter on PDF pages 85-86 explicitly permits a STRING routine result and shows toupper returning CHR. Routine-return descriptions on 93/521 broadly permit types except FILE/PATH/vision. The STRING type entry on 563 says STRING values cannot be returned by functions. These statements conflict within the same Rev N manual.
unresolved.disposition: E_RETURN_TYPE is retained for STRING functions pending discriminating release-specific compiler/runtime evidence. No implementation is inferred from either manual statement alone.

literal_update.boundary: Doubled ASCII apostrophes decode inside one physical STRING token before logical-value checks. Existing quoted-WRITE, writable value and STRING-result guards remain.

manual: FANUC KAREL Reference Manual, MARRC75KR07091E Rev N
